Production planning
Look up a finished-good SKU to see whether there's an opportunity to open a work order, based on current raw material stock.
Raw material requirements are estimated from historical work orders (raw material consumed ÷ finished units produced). Raw materials tracked by weight often use a _KG suffix (e.g. RCF vs RCF_KG) — each is matched to its own stock record and unit of measure, so figures for the two variants aren't combined. For SKUs currently at stockout risk, the "Opportunity" badge is replaced by the same incoming-shipment verdict shown in Supply Coverage (hover it for full purchase order detail). "Covered" means a shipment is already on the way and no new work order is needed. Other SKUs keep the simple stock-based Yes/No check.

"Suggested WO qty" targets 2 months of stock coverage based on monthly sales; it's capped by nothing here, so if it's larger than "Max units producible" you don't have enough raw material on hand or incoming to fully close the gap in one work order.

Supply coverage
For every SKU at stockout risk — is a work order actually needed, or is something already on the way?
Built from the Open PO Report. For each SKU at stockout risk, checks whether incoming purchase orders (finished goods or raw materials, approved only) will resolve the shortfall — and whether they'll land before the earliest ship-cancel date on open orders. "Ship cancel" used is the earliest one across all open sales orders for that SKU.

"Suggested WO qty" targets 2 months of stock coverage: (2 × monthly sales) − (net position + qty already in production + incoming finished goods). Shown as 0 when that target is already met. SKUs without a monthly sales figure show "No sales data".
